mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility rose for two consecutive weeks (11.7 to 13.6 to 17.0) while RETAIL_REC fell, indicating renewed stay-at-home compliance consistent with tightening public health restrictions. This behavioral shift is expected to further suppress discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises for 2 consecutive weeks by more than 1.5 points each week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 11.7 to 17.0 over last two weeks while RETAIL_REC fell from -21.3 to -37.9
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean rises above its 28-day trailing mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to climb, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC move together because transit usage proxies for out-of-home trip generation that includes retail visits. The co-movement observed across all four weeks (both troughing at t-3w and declining again at t-0w) implies TRANSIT's downward trend will continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC both declined from t-2w to t-0w (TRANSIT -60.3 to -71.7, RETAIL_REC -21.3 to -37.9)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean increases while TRANSIT remains flat or declines further, the always-on trend linkage is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects resumption of commuting routines, which generates incidental retail trips (lunch, errands, after-work shopping) that lift RETAIL_REC. The interaction of both series rising together is a stronger signal than either alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase by at least 5 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -36.1 to -20.4 between t-3w and t-2w alongside TRANSIT improving from -74.4 to -60.3
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise concurrently but RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean does not exceed its trailing mean, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows volatile but generally suppressed levels consistent with Melbourne's cooler season, reducing outdoor substitution activity that would otherwise divert trips away from indoor retail; however, persistently negative PARKS levels combined with deep RETAIL_REC negativity indicate an overall subdued mobility season that will keep RETAIL_REC low through the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained between -50.4 and -26.9 across all four weeks, never approaching baseline
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility recovers toward baseline (>-10) without a corresponding rise in RETAIL_REC, the seasonal substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 10 points, as seen between t-1w and t-0w (-63.9 to -71.7), signals an abrupt policy tightening event (e.g., stricter stay-at-home orders). Such shocks are expected to immediately suppress RETAIL_REC in the following week before any broader trend stabilizes.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -63.9 to -71.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean one week after a >10-point TRANSIT drop is not lower than the week preceding the drop, the threshold mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained close to baseline (within ±5 points) across all four weeks while RETAIL_REC stays deeply negative, indicating a lockdown steady-state where essential activity is permitted but discretionary retail remains restricted. This regime is expected to persist, keeping RETAIL_REC flat-to-lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within ±5 points of baseline for 2+ weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -20
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged only from -5.4 to 1.3 across all four weeks while RETAIL_REC stayed between -47.4 and -21.3
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean rises substantially (by more than 10 points) while GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline, the steady-state hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises at the same time WORKPLACES mobility falls, it signals a joint behavioral shift toward home-based living and away from commuting, doubly confirming restriction tightening. This combined signal predicts a sharper near-term decline in RETAIL_REC than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases week-on-week while WORKPLACES simultaneously decreases week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:between t-1w and t-0w RESIDENTIAL rose from 13.6 to 17.0 while WORKPLACES fell from -23.3 to -31.0
failure_condition: If this joint pattern occurs but RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean does not fall relative to its trailing mean, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility improving relative to its trough (from -50.4 to -26.9) reflects growing outdoor activity that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation trips, independent of policy regime. This always-on substitution effect predicts RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed even as overall mobility partially recovers.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -50.4 at t-3w to -26.9 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC did not show a matching sustained recovery
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean rises in tandem with continued PARKS improvement, the substitution mechanism is rejected.
